decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee at its meeting today decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed reduced the benchmark federal funds rate by 50 basis points down to 4 percent.

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 50 basis point reduction in the discount rate to 3-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: The separate discount rate charged to banks was also lowered by 50 basis points to 3-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Investment in capital equipment, however, has continued to decline.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that business spending on equipment has kept falling.

changes.quote: With pressures on labor and product markets easing, inflation is expected to remain contained.
changes.explanation: Easing pressures in markets led the Fed to expect contained inflation.

changes.quote: Although measured productivity growth stalled in the first quarter, the impressive underlying rate of increase that developed in recent years appears to be largely intact, supporting longer-term prospects.
changes.explanation: Even though first quarter productivity stalled, long-term underlying growth trends remain supportive.

tone_quotes.quote: Investment in capital equipment, however, has continued to decline.

The Committee continues to believe that against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.63% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.5% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.14% would rise by about $8.11 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.4%, and employers added an average of -82k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.2% over the past year (April 2001); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -1.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -1 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Committee remains focused on economic weakness as the primary risk going forward. Future meetings will continue to evaluate incoming data on business spending and labor markets.
